analyst_view.overall: This Madeira derby, the first top-flight meeting in five years, sets 15th against 13th: Mitchell van der Gaag's Marítimo have 8 points from 10 games and no league win since 16 August, while João Henriques's Nacional have 10 points from 11 and two 1-0 wins in their last three. For Marítimo, left-back Paulo Henrique has recovered and is expected to start (Lusa), but Rafael Fernandes and Yellu Santiago are still out; the numbers only list Yellu. For Nacional, A Bola (26 Nov, the newest report) says Ulisses and Wesley Gasolina are fit and in the squad, Liziero is doubtful and Léo Santos and Filipe Soares are out, so the numbers, which still treat Gasolina as missing, are slightly too pessimistic about Nacional's attack; one day earlier Sports Mole still had Ulisses out, so this rests mainly on one report. Nacional have not won at the Barreiros since 2011-12, the ground is close to sold out, and Miguel Fonseca (Porto FA) referees, with his short record (3.5 cards a game in 2 games) already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and take about 22% off Nacional's side for Léo Santos, Liziero and Gasolina. A Bola now reports Gasolina fit, which gives back roughly 0.06 goals the numbers took off (Liziero stays doubtful, so his cut holds), and that halves yesterday's lean. What still pulls down is a tense, full-house derby between two sides near the bottom, Marítimo's weak scoring (9 in 10) and Nacional's run of one-goal games, so I lean only slightly lower, to about 2.35.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, already adding a little for Marítimo's recent corner count (+2.6%) and taking a little off Nacional's (-2.0%). Marítimo at home in front of a full house should push forward, and Paulo Henrique's return gives them their usual left-back, but Nacional's likely shape (Henriques says they worked on set pieces) does not clearly change the count, so I stay at 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards: they take 7.8% off because Nacional have been booked less than usual lately, and 3.7% for referee Miguel Fonseca's low record (3.5 a game, only 2 games), and they do not treat this as a derby. It is the Madeira derby, both clubs are near the relegation zone, Marítimo's coach calls it a turning point and the ground is close to sold out, none of which the numbers see, so I lean higher by 10%, to about 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots and already cut Nacional's side by 7.8% for their low recent shot count. Marítimo should have more of the ball at home, while Nacional under Henriques won 1-0 twice and may sit deeper; Gasolina being fit helps Nacional a little going forward. These pull in both directions, so I stay at 25.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target and already add 4.2% to Marítimo because Nacional have conceded plenty on target lately. Marítimo's finishing has been poor and Nacional's Liziero is still doubtful, but the numbers' ratings and missing list already reflect both, and I have put the tight-derby point on goals, so I stay at 9.7.
